## Status and limitations

The prior release phases remain integrated. Upgrade Phase 6 rewrites the public story around one canonical Driftwatch sample: the landing page now has one primary action, a four-stage workflow, a coherent abandoned-open-source sample, a direct OpenCode explanation, local setup and privacy, and a short FAQ. The non-interactive idea-to-tool recommendation block was removed, and the technical sample disclosure moved under details. Upgrade Phase 5 remains the focused workshop: one main task, a collapsible outline, contextual Activity & results, editable Project memory, a compact model/connection header, and lazy Advanced diagnostics. Schema v7 is unchanged.

Known limitations:

- The application is a trusted single-project tool, not a multi-tenant sandbox. Remote imports are public HTTPS clones into a managed local directory; private/authenticated repositories, shared-host isolation, arbitrary Maker access to selected repositories, and remote browser-to-local pairing remain deferred.
- Maker edits only `UB_DATA_DIR/demo-workspace`; the Node check is not an OS sandbox.
- Generated section review supports a deliberately small, safe Markdown subset (headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, links, tables, and code), not full CommonMark or raw HTML. Contract validation checks structure and topic coverage, not prose quality.
- Model availability, pricing, quota, training terms, and billing are controlled by OpenCode/provider. The spending limit only checks cost OpenCode reports after a session; unknown-price providers may bill before that value is visible.
- The workspace privacy preference records intent; the app cannot attest every provider's training/retention contract. Provider rejections that mention training/data policy are explained as `PROVIDER_DATA_POLICY`.
- Advanced diagnostics load only when opened. Permission polling is best-effort; a pending request remains visible in Activity & results and the contextual permission alert, but a provider-side change can lag by one refresh interval.
- Backboard is not integrated and no partner category is claimed for installation alone. Sentry is configured but live release/source-map/trace verification requires authorized credentials and a deployment.
- No public hosted URL, recorded video, published article, or submission is asserted by this repository.
- A real recorded demonstration and final submission packaging remain separate acceptance work.

| Private workshop | `private-hosted` | Password-protected | Loopback child | Private persistent disk | `render.yaml` |

Both serve the same build:

- `/` — landing page;
- `/demo` — labeled recorded Driftwatch sample;
- `/workshop` — real workshop (read-only notice in demo mode);
- `/api/*` — validated API.

A hosted instance is **not** a public sandbox, a remote mount of a visitor's checkout, proof of free-model availability, or a substitute for the local real-execution demonstration.

## Hosted sample behavior

`UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted-demo` serves the public guided example without OpenCode, provider credentials, a repository, a session token, or visitor persistence:

| Behavior | Hosted sample |
|---|---|
| Routes | `/`, `/demo`, `/workshop` public; `/api/health` and `/api/mode` public |
| API reads | `/api/project` and `/api/export` return the versioned fixture |
| API writes | Every non-GET `/api/*` request returns `403 DEMO_READ_ONLY` before a body is parsed |
| Session token | `/api/session` returns `403`; no token is issued |
| OpenCode | `/api/opencode/*` is unavailable; no connection object is constructed |
| Connection | `/api/connection` returns a read-only demo status with no engine address |
| Repository | None. Sample workspace is `demo://driftwatch` |
| Persistence | No visitor state is written; reload returns the same sample |
| Inference | Zero model/provider calls |
| Reset | Changes only client playback state |

Do not set `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD` or start `render-start.ts` for the demo. Use `npm start` with `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted-demo`; `render.demo.yaml` does that on a free service. The server rejection is independent of the UI.

```bash
npm run build
UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted-demo \
UB_HOST=127.0.0.1 \
UB_PORT=4319 \
UB_DATA_DIR=/tmp/opencode/ub-demo-smoke \
node --import tsx src/server/start.ts
```

Then verify:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4319/api/health
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4319/api/project
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4319/api/session          # 403

The Phase 9 smoke run passed these checks and confirmed `/demo` returns HTML.

```

The application itself prefers a compatible global `opencode` on `PATH`; otherwise it resolves the lockfile-installed binary. If you install globally instead:

```bash
# npm on Linux or macOS
npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.0.32
opencode --version

# Homebrew on macOS

```

A full model call was not repeated during the Phase 9 gate. The Phase 9 compatibility probe verified server version, catalog access, and disposable session create/read/remove without inference.

### Platform diagnostics

Run these before opening a support issue:

```bash
npm run diagnose:platform   # executable, source, version, platform support, permission
npm run smoke:opencode      # starts the resolved server, reads /api/info, stops it
```

The diagnostic emits one of:

| Code | Meaning | Repair |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENCODE_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` | Host is not Linux x64, macOS arm64, or macOS x64 | Run on a supported host; do not claim the current host as supported. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_MISSING` | No usable `opencode` on `PATH` and no materialized `@opencode/cli` binary | Run `npm ci`; if install scripts were disabled, reinstall with scripts enabled. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_PERMISSION_DENIED` | A candidate exists but is not executable by this user | Fix ownership/mode or reinstall without `sudo`. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE` | Major version is not 2, or no version was reported | Install `@opencode/cli@2.0.32` or the matching Homebrew tap. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_VERSION_UNTESTED` | A different 2.x patch was found | Use 2.0.32 for the tested surface, or run the live diagnostic. |
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_START_FAILED` | The server exited before answering `/api/info` | Check the port, data/config directory permissions, and the CLI version. |

No diagnostic prints the executable path, credentials, prompts, or model output.

### The engine badge says unreachable

1. Confirm OpenCode is listening: `curl http://127.0.0.1:4096/`.
2. Check `/api/connection` with the session token.
3. Confirm `OPENCODE_BASE_URL` matches.
4. Confirm `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` matches the server. The wizard uses Basic auth with OpenCode's fixed `opencode` username.
5. Run `npm run diagnose:platform` and `npm run smoke:opencode` to separate CLI resolution from server/network problems.
6. Restart the API after changing `.env`.

### The OpenCode executable is missing or not executable

`npm run diagnose:platform` returns `OPENCODE_CLI_MISSING` or `OPENCODE_CLI_PERMISSION_DENIED`. Run `npm ci` with install scripts enabled. On macOS/Linux, avoid `sudo`; fix ownership on the install directory instead. `@opencode/cli` materializes its native binary during postinstall, so `--ignore-scripts` installs are incomplete.

### Unsupported architecture

`npm run diagnose:platform` returns `OPENCODE_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED`. Supported hosts are Linux x64, macOS Apple Silicon, and macOS Intel. Linux ARM64, Windows, and 32-bit hosts are not tested or claimed. Use one of the supported hosts or a remote allowlisted OpenCode server from the supported application host.

### OpenCode CLI version is incompatible

The resolver reports `OPENCODE_CLI_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE` when the major version is not 2 or no version can be parsed. Install the pinned CLI with `npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.0.32`, or on macOS run `brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2`. A different 2.x patch resolves but shows `OPENCODE_CLI_VERSION_UNTESTED`.

### OpenCode server failed to start

`npm run smoke:opencode` reports `OPENCODE_SERVER_START_FAILED` when the server exits before answering `/api/info`. Confirm port 4096 or the chosen port is free, the XDG/data directories are writable, and a compatible CLI is selected. The smoke script starts a disposable server, makes no model call, and stops it automatically.

# OpenCode integration contract

**Status:** Implemented and locally verified on Linux x64; macOS Apple Silicon and macOS Intel are covered by the CI matrix.
**Owner:** Engineering/integration.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 against Platform Phase 7 and the Phase 5 focused-workshop/OpenCode-controls surface.

This document describes the supported OpenCode surface, not every endpoint OpenCode exposes. OpenCode remains the owner of inference, the agent loop, tools, permissions, and native sessions.

## Supported versions, client, and hosts

| Component | Tested value | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode server | `2.0.32` | Major `2` is accepted. A different `2.x` version is shown as `degraded` with an explicit untested-version warning. Major `1.x`, unparseable versions, and other majors are `incompatible_version`; discovery stops. |
| OpenCode CLI package | `@opencode/cli` `2.0.32` | Official cross-platform package pinned in the lockfile. Its postinstall selects the native binary for the host. |
| `@opencode/client` | `2.0.32` | Exact lockfile version, matched to the pinned server. |
| Node.js | `>=22.14` | Application runtime. |
| Server host | loopback by default | A remote target must use HTTPS, be explicitly allowlisted, and pass DNS/IP policy. |
| Local host platform | Linux x64, macOS arm64, macOS x64 | Declared supported. Linux is verified in this checkout; macOS is gated by the CI jobs below. Windows, Linux ARM64, and 32-bit hosts are not claimed. |

### CLI resolution and Render isolation

`src/server/opencode/executable.ts` is the only runtime resolver. It:

1. honors an explicit `UB_OPENCODE_EXECUTABLE`;
2. prefers a compatible global `opencode` found on `PATH` (npm, Homebrew, or a package manager install);
3. falls back to the lockfile-installed `node_modules/@opencode/cli/bin/opencode.exe`;
4. probes `--version` and requires major `2`, warning when the patch is not `2.0.32`;
5. rejects unsupported platforms before probing anything.

The Render/private-hosted supervisor (`src/server/render-start.ts`) uses the same resolver. Its only Render-specific behavior is environment configuration (`OPENCODE_DATA_HOME`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_HOME`, `OPENCODE_PORT`, and the loopback bind). Local development never starts that supervisor and never depends on a Linux executable path. Default XDG locations are derived from `UB_DATA_DIR` or the host temporary directory, not a hardcoded `/tmp` or `/var/data` path.

### Runtime diagnostics

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENCODE_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` | error | Host is not Linux x64, macOS arm64, or macOS x64. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_MISSING` | error | No usable executable on `PATH` or in the local package. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_PERMISSION_DENIED` | error | Candidate exists but cannot be executed by this user. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE` | error | Major version is not `2`, or no version was reported. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_VERSION_UNTESTED` | warning | A different `2.x` patch is in use. |
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_START_FAILED` | error | The child server exited before answering `/api/info`. |

Diagnostics contain no executable path, credential, prompt, or model output. `npm run diagnose:platform` prints resolution only; `npm run smoke:opencode` starts the resolved server with disposable XDG directories, reads `/api/info` with a generated in-memory password, and stops it without a prompt or model call.

## Private hosted configuration

`render.yaml` defines one paid Linux x64 Node web service:

| Setting | Value/behavior |
|---|---|
| Runtime | Node 22.14 |
| Plan | `0.5c-512mb`; persistent disk required |
| Build | `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` |
| Start | `npm run start:render` |
| Health check | `/api/health` (public, minimal) |
| Disk | 1 GB at `/var/data` |
| Host binding | `UB_HOST=0.0.0.0` |
| Deployment mode | `REDACTED` |
| Data | `UB_DATA_DIR=/var/data/unfinished-business` |
| Access | `UB_ACCESS_USERNAME` + generated `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD` |
| Session token | Generated `UB_SESSION_TOKEN` |
| OpenCode | Generated `OPENCODE_PASSWORD`; loopback `http://127.0.0.1:4096` |
| OpenCode storage | `/var/data/xdg-data`, `/var/data/xdg-config` |
| Origin policy | `RENDER_EXTERNAL_HOSTNAME` supplies the public HTTPS origin |
| Sentry | DSNs and auth token supplied as sync-false secrets |

`npm run start:render` starts the pinned OpenCode baseline binary on loopback, then the Hono server. It forwards termination to both and exits if OpenCode exits unexpectedly. It does not require a build tool on the runtime disk; the binary is pinned in the lockfile.

The private service is **not compatible with Render's free plan** because it needs a persistent disk and enough memory for OpenCode.

## Environment variables

Canonical mode is `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (`local`, `private-hosted`, `hosted-demo`). `UB_MODE` remains a compatibility alias; the legacy `hosted-private` spelling maps to `private-hosted`.

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` | Yes on Render | `private-hosted` for `render.yaml`; `hosted-demo` for `render.demo.yaml`. |
| `UB_HOST` | Yes on Render | `0.0.0.0` behind the proxy. Local mode must stay loopback. |
| `UB_PUBLIC_URL` | Private hosted | Explicit HTTPS origin. Render derives it from `RENDER_EXTERNAL_HOSTNAME`. |
| `UB_ALLOWED_HOSTS` / `UB_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | Optional | Additional comma-separated host/origin entries. The public URL host/origin is added automatically. |
| `UB_TRUST_PROXY` | Hosted | Defaults to true in hosted modes; trust `X-Forwarded-*` only behind a controlled proxy. |
| `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD` | Private hosted | Basic Auth password; the server refuses to start without it. |
| `UB_ACCESS_USERNAME` | Recommended | Defaults to `unfinished-business`. |
| `UB_SESSION_TOKEN` | Private hosted | Required; generated by Render. |
| `UB_DATA_DIR` | Yes | Dedicated persistent directory, e.g. `/var/data/unfinished-business`. |
| `UB_MAX_SESSION_COST_USD` | Optional | `unlimited` (default), `disabled`, or `0` for no app ceiling; a positive value sets a deployment-wide USD ceiling. A project limit can be stricter; cost is checked against OpenCode's reported value. |
| `OPENCODE_BASE_URL` | Yes | Keep `http://127.0.0.1:4096` for the private child. Remote targets require HTTPS + allowlist. |
| `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` | Private hosted | Required by `render-start.ts`; passed to OpenCode as both `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` and `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`. |
| `OPENCODE_DATA_HOME` / `OPENCODE_CONFIG_HOME` | Private hosted | XDG paths on the persistent disk. |
| `UB_OPENCODE_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | Remote only | Explicit HTTPS host allowlist. |
| `UB_OPENCODE_ALLOWED_PORTS` | Optional | Comma-separated port allowlist. |
| `UB_OPENCODE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK` | Rare | Only when a private network target is intended. |
| `SENTRY_DSN` / `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` | Optional | Public project identifiers, not auth tokens. |
| `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` | Source maps only | Build secret; never `VITE_`-prefixed or committed. |
| `SENTRY_ORG` / `SENTRY_PROJECT` / `SENTRY_URL` | Source maps only | Sentry project/region configuration. |

Do not set `SENTRY_RELEASE` manually on Render; both server and browser derive `unfinished-business@<RENDER_GIT_COMMIT>`.

## Reviewable deployment procedure

No step below was executed in Phase 9. Deployment is a separate authorized action.

1. Push the release commit to the intended repository. Do not push from this worktree without authorization.
2. In Render, create a Blueprint from `render.yaml` (private) or `render.demo.yaml` (public demo).
3. Review the service plan, region, disk mount, health check, and generated secrets before applying.
4. For the private service, supply the Sentry DSNs and optional auth token. Confirm the build fails rather than deploys without source maps when `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is present and required.
5. Apply. Confirm the disk is mounted at `/var/data` and is not the build directory.
6. Wait for `/api/health` to return `{"status":"ok","service":"unfinished-business"}`.
7. For the private service, open the URL and sign in with `unfinished-business` and the generated `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD`. Confirm HTTPS and the host/origin policy.
8. For the demo, confirm `/api/session` is 403, `/api/project` returns the fixture, a mutation is `403 DEMO_READ_ONLY`, and `/api/engine` reports no OpenCode connection.
9. For the private service, open `/workshop`, run a connection check, and confirm the engine status. Do not claim a model call succeeded until the provider actually returns one.
10. Confirm logs contain correlation IDs but no passwords, prompts, bodies, provider keys, or local paths.
11. Verify Sentry release/source-map association only when authorized credentials and a deployment exist. Check the event release matches the uploaded maps and deploy.
12. Keep the public URL, deployment result, and any partner/competition claim out of documentation until separately verified.

**Date:** 2026-11-01
**Status:** Platform Phase 7 implemented; deployment, publication, and submission remain outside this phase.

## What changed

### Platform Phase 7 — macOS support

- Replaced the Linux-only `@opencode/cli-linux-x64-baseline` dependency with the official cross-platform **`@opencode/cli` 2.0.32**, still pinned with `@opencode/client` 2.0.32 in the lockfile.
- Added one platform-aware resolver. It prefers an explicit `UB_OPENCODE_EXECUTABLE`, then a compatible global `opencode` on `PATH` (npm, Homebrew, or another package manager), then the lockfile-installed binary. An incompatible global install is skipped so the pinned local CLI can still run.
- Added distinct diagnostics for an unsupported architecture, missing executable, non-executable install, incompatible CLI major, untested 2.x patch, and server start failure. Diagnostics never print executable paths, credentials, prompts, or model output.
- Declared support for **Linux x64**, **macOS Apple Silicon**, and **macOS Intel**. Windows, Linux ARM64, and 32-bit hosts are unsupported and report `OPENCODE_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED`.
- Kept the Render supervisor, but it now shares the resolver. Render-specific storage and port values come from environment variables rather than a hardcoded Linux executable path.
- Replaced the Playwright `/tmp` data directory with the host temporary directory and added standard macOS Chrome/Chromium application paths.
- Hardened workspace validation for macOS: `/Users`, `/Volumes`, `/System`, `/private`, `/private/tmp`, `/private/var/tmp`, and `/private/var/folders` are broad roots, and the resolved host temporary root is rejected even through the macOS `/var` → `/private/var` alias.
- Updated the setup tabs and local guide: no user-facing command names a Linux-only package path, and npm plus Homebrew installation commands are documented.
- Added `npm run diagnose:platform` (resolution only) and `npm run smoke:opencode` (disposable server start and `/api/info` check; no prompt or model call).
- Added a CI matrix for `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-15`, and `macos-15-intel`, each covering dependency install, CLI resolution, typecheck, tests, build, workspace path safety, and the OpenCode smoke test.
- No schema change or migration is required; schema v7 and saved projects are unchanged.

# Tool and capability catalog

**Status:** Current release inventory.
**Owner:** Engineering.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01.

This catalog distinguishes what the product **uses** and what is only a **documented future possibility**. A listed tool is not an install, account, endorsement, or partner-category proof.

## Core tools

| Tool | Role | Status | Evidence/limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenCode 2.0.32 | Agent loop, model access, native tools, permissions, sessions, interruption | **Integrated foundation** | Exact client/server pin; production code uses the official client through the safe network layer. Live compatibility probe passed without inference. |
| OpenCode model catalog | Any model the connected account reports as available | **Integrated; model-dependent** | New projects default to all accessible models. Free/local-only policy and optional spending limits are available. Paid/unknown-price routes require explicit confirmation; no silent substitution. |
| Node.js 22.14+ | Runtime, build, and bounded Node check | **Required** | Tested on 22.22.1; `engines` minimum 22.14. |
| React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 8 | Browser interface and build | **Integrated** | Production build and bundle budget pass. |
| Hono 4 + `@hono/node-server` | HTTP API and static serving | **Integrated** | Security middleware, validation, SSE, and static containment are tested. |
| Zod 4 | Shared request/state/output validation | **Integrated** | Workflow schema v7, explicit v1–v6 migration, project-source/Oracle intake, reviewable candidate revisions, section contracts, model policy, provider-error, and engine/discovery contracts. |
| Motion 14 + Lucide | Purposeful motion and icons | **Integrated** | Free libraries only; reduced-motion fallback tested. No second animation framework. |

## Verification and operations tools

| Tool | Role | Status | Evidence/limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node test runner | Unit/integration/component tests | **Integrated** | 186 passing tests. |
| Playwright 1.62 | Visual, keyboard, contrast, zoom, reduced-motion, overflow, and canonical-sample tests | **Integrated** | 20 passing tests with committed snapshots; uses system Chromium. |
| `scripts/check-budget.mjs` | Production bundle/asset budget | **Integrated** | Passes: initial JS 201.3 KiB gzip, all JS 279.9 KiB (290 KiB budget), CSS 17.0 KiB (18 KiB budget), hero 581.2 KiB. |
| `scripts/preflight.mjs` | Read-only environment diagnostic | **Integrated** | Checks toolchain, DNS, loopback, OpenCode CLI/help, Git reads, Entire status. Not an integration proof. |
| `scripts/opencode-live-diagnostic.ts` | Opt-in compatibility probe | **Integrated; run in Phase 9** | Server 2.0.32, catalog, disposable session create/read/remove. No prompt/model call. |
| Render | Optional demo or private hosting | **Documented; not deployed** | `render.demo.yaml` and `render.yaml` reviewed statically. No live URL asserted. |
| GitHub Actions | Typecheck/test/build quality gate | **Configured** | `.github/workflows/sentry-release.yml` runs the quality gate; Render owns production source-map upload. |

## Observability and development evidence

| Tool | Role | Status | Evidence/limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sentry Node/browser SDKs | Optional errors, traces, replay, profiling, metadata-only agent spans | **Configured; live release proof not run** | SDK collection is disabled for prompts/bodies/headers/identity; redaction is tested. A live event/release/source-map/trace check needs authorized credentials and a deployment. |
| Entire | Development-session capture and checkpoints | **Development record only** | Repository has Entire hooks/checkpoints from earlier phases. It is not a runtime product feature and no public transcript is shared. |
| Backboard R-CLI | Candidate build-process contribution | **Not integrated** | No API key/tooling in this environment; no session, diff, check, or category claim. |

There is no landing-page idea-to-tool recommender in this release. The previous static table was removed in Upgrade Phase 6 because it was not interactive or capability-driven.
